References / Illustration / 103

Airbnb illustration guidelines, “Your Face Here” (Jennifer Hom)

Airbnb’s head of illustration explains its 2018 illustration redesign, which kept flat, lightweight figures but rejected the rainbow-colored skin of the tech style.

Source
Airbnb Design (Medium): Jennifer Hom, “Your Face Here”, 18 December 2018
Creator
Jennifer Hom, Airbnb
Made
2017–2018
Style
Corporate Memphis (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Warm, inclusive, grounded
Evidence
Read the article text through a Wayback Machine copy; medium.com returned HTTP 403 to scripts. The article images did not load in that copy, so no illustration was inspected.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Hom joined Airbnb in October 2017 to redesign its illustration style. She lists four principles: “grounded, scalable, lightweight, and diverse”, and says the style is “fairly minimal and lightweight” with “intentional white space”. Airbnb Design.

She describes a common solution in tech illustration as “a metaphor for diversity through rainbow-colored figures … colored in red, blue, yellow, orange, purple, and green. Put simply, they’re not real.” She tried this in early drafts and rejected it. Airbnb Design.

She also rejects “cartoon people outlined in blue or grey”, and asks for reference photos for every person drawn and for different races, ages, abilities, and body types. Airbnb Design.

Why it belongs

The article is a contemporary insider’s description of the style’s central device, non-natural skin, as a way to avoid questions of race. It helps separate the style from other flat tech illustration of the same years.

Borrow

When figures must represent real users, use a real range of skin tones and body types; keep the flat fills and white space.

What to review next

  • Inspect the article’s illustrations in a browser and upgrade the evidence level if they show figures.
